- Monthly pension of Rs. 2000
- Monthly pension of Rs. 3000
- Monthly pension of Rs. 4000
- Monthly pension of Rs. 5000
- Central Government will co-contribute 50% of the total yearly contribution or Rs. 1000 per annum, whichever is lower, for the period of 5 Years in the account of subscribers who join the scheme up to 31st December, 2015 and who are not a member of any Statutory Social Scheme and not an income tax payer.
- Subscribers joining APY scheme at an early stage of age would be required to pay lesser monthly subscription amount as compared to the subscriber joining at a later age as illustrated in the above table.

title: PM-Vishwakarma Scheme — Empowering Traditional Artisans and Craftspeople in India. (Bank of Baroda)
body:
Empowering Traditional Artisans and Craftspeople in India.:
- Apply for the PM-Vishwakarma Scheme today and take a step towards enhancing your craft, expanding your market reach, and securing a prosperous future!
- The PM-Vishwakarma Scheme is tailored to provide a variety of benefits to artisans, whether they are self-employed or aspiring to start their own small-scale ventures. This scheme not only aids in the preservation of cultural practices, traditional skills, and the Guru-shishya parampara but also offers artisans an identity and recognition.

title: PM-Vishwakarma Scheme — PM-Vishwakarma Scheme : Purpose (Bank of Baroda)
body:
PM-Vishwakarma Scheme : Purpose:
- The PM-Vishwakarma Scheme is a transformative initiative fully funded by the Government of India, aimed at empowering traditional artisans and craftspeople through comprehensive support for their growth and development.
- This Central Sector scheme seeks to enhance the quality and reach of artisans' products and services while integrating them into both domestic and global value chains.
- It provides financial support, skill training, and various benefits directly from the central government to help artisans thrive.
- At Bank of Baroda, we are dedicated to supporting the Government of India's initiatives aimed at empowering artisans/ craftsmen through the PM-Vishwakarma Scheme. The Bank stands firm in its commitment to fostering entrepreneurship and contributing to the overall growth of the MSME sector in India.
- For more information, please visit the nearest Bank of Baroda branch or contact our Customer Support team.

title: PM-Vishwakarma Scheme — PM-Vishwakarma Scheme : Benefits (Bank of Baroda)
body:
PM-Vishwakarma Scheme : Benefits:
- As per PM Vishwakarma guidelines, the scheme is designed to offer end-to-end support to artisans and craftspeople through the following components:
- Recognition and Certification: Artisans receive official recognition from the Government of India for their craftsmanship through the PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card, which enhances their credibility and marketability within the industry.
- Skill Upgradation : Benefit from skill training provided by government-nominated training centers to enhance your craft.
- Toolkit Incentive : Receive up to ₹15,000 for modern tools through e-vouchers provided by the government.
- Credit Support: To strengthen and support the skills of traditional artisans and craftspeople, this scheme facilitates access to affordable credit. Beneficiaries to complete skill assessment and necessary training from Government of India before they qualify for the credit support.
- Incentive for Digital Transactions : Earn ₹1 per transaction incentive for up to 100 transactions monthly, with direct transfers to your bank account.
- Marketing Support : Gain government support in quality certification, branding, e-commerce platform listing, trade fair participation, and market linkages to promote your products.

title: PM-Vishwakarma Scheme — PM-Vishwakarma Scheme : Features (Bank of Baroda)
body:
PM-Vishwakarma Scheme : Features:
- The scheme includes several key features as under:
- Collateral-Free Loans : Access collateral-free Enterprise Development Loans of up to ₹3 lakh in two tranches: the first tranche allows for a loan of up to ₹1 lakh with a maximum tenure of 18 months, while the second tranche offers up to ₹2 lakh with a maximum tenure of 30 months.
- Support for Women Artisans and Marginalized Groups: The scheme empowers women artisans, fostering gender equality, and encouraging their participation in the workforce. Additionally, it aims to uplift individuals from marginalized or underserved communities, including Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes (OBCs), persons with disabilities, transgender individuals, as well as residents of Northeastern states, island territories, and hilly regions of India.
- Insurance Coverage : The scheme provides access to insurance schemes that provide financial security against unforeseen events, ensuring livelihoods of artisans are protected.

title: PM-Vishwakarma Scheme — PM-Vishwakarma Scheme : Eligibility (Bank of Baroda)
body:
PM-Vishwakarma Scheme : Eligibility:
- To qualify for the PM-Vishwakarma Scheme, applicants must meet the following criteria:
- Must be an Indian resident and self-employed in a traditional craft or trade.
- Minimum age of 18 years at the time of registration.
- Should not have availed loans under similar credit-based schemes of the Central or State Government for self-employment/business development in the past 5 years. However, fully repaid loans under MUDRA or SVANidhi, are eligible.
- Only one member per family (spouse or unmarried children) can apply.
- Government employees and their family members are not eligible.
- Must have Standard Accounts as indicated in the Credit Bureau Report at the time of application.
- Applicants must be KYC compliant with our bank.
- Only applications submitted through the PM Vishwakarma portal shall be considered.

title: bob Start-up Current Account — bob Start-up Current Account : Fees & Charges (Bank of Baroda)
body:
bob Start-up Current Account : Fees & Charges:
- After 2 years from date of opening of current account, minimum QAB to be maintained is Rs.75,000/-. Service Charge of Rs 1000/-+ GST for Non-maintenance of QAB.
- Applicable to Base Branch, Local Non-Base Branches:- Beyond Cash Deposit of Rs. 50000/- Or above 10 packets i.e. 1000 pieces of notes of any denominations taken together, whichever is higher charges will be levied as under – Above 10 packets – i.e. 1000 pieces of notes charges will be levied @ Rs.10/- per packet or a part thereof. (Min. Rs.10/- Maxi. Rs.10000/- (per day per Txn.)
- Applicable to Outstation Branches:- Chargeable in case of cash deposit in excess of Rs 25000/- per day per account at Rs 2.50 per thousand or part thereof at outstation branch.
- At Cash Machines: Cash deposit with debit card is allowed up to Rs.2,00,000/- (2 Lacs) per day where PAN is registered and Rs.49,999/- where PAN is not be registered in account. Card less transaction (by feeding account number) is allowed up to Rs. 20,000/- per day. Fake note, Suspicious Note is impounded and receipt will be given to the customer. Torne/Mutilated/Taped notes are not accepted by this machine.
- Withdrawal allowed by cheque only. No upper limit for cash withdrawing at base branch. At local non-base branch and outstation branches Cash withdrawal up to Rs.25,000/- per day per account is free of charges thereafter service charges is levied. Third party cash payment at non-base branches is not allowed.
- Statement of Account is provided twice a month free of cost.
- A/c cannot be transferred from one Branch to another Branch. For closure of Current account within one year @ Rs.600/-+ GST will be deducted.
- Free for 1st 2 years from the date of account opening, thereafter 50% of applicable charges.

title: MSME Loan (Bank of Baroda)
body:
- Government of India vide Gazette notification S.O. 2119(E) dated 26.06.2020 (Annexure-I) has notified revised criteria for classifying the enterprises as micro, small and medium enterprises and the revised definition is effective from 1st of July 2020.
- The value of plant and Machinery or Equipment for all purposes of the Notification No. S.O. 2.t19(E) dated June 26, 2020 and for all the enterprises shall mean the Written Down Value (WDV) as at the end of the Financial Year as defined in the Income Tax Act and not cost of acquisition or original price, which was applicable in the context of the earlier classification criteria .
- The investment in plant and machinery or equipment does not exceed ₹.2.5 crores rupees and turnover does not exceed ₹.10 crores.

title: Supply Chain Finance (Bank of Baroda)
body:
Supply Chain Finance:
- Supply Chain Finance (SCF) is a short term working capital finance to DEALERS/ VENDORS (“Spoke”) having business relationships with LARGE CORPORATE (“Anchor”) to optimise working capital requirements of both Spoke & Anchor. Supply Chain Finance is a fine blend of Bill discounting & overdraft product with the essence to optimise finance and flexibility for the customer. All transactions are linked to a base document (invoice) between the Anchor & the Spoke.
Inventory Funding:
- The Buyers need not to have a formal dealership agreement for Inventory Funding Facility.
Dealer Finance:
- Our Dealer Finance program provides Working Capital Credit facilities for Dealers/ Distributors/ Channel partners of large corporates for procurement of inventory from large corporates.
Vendor Finance (Limit on Vendor):
- Our Vendor Finance program provides Working Capital Credit facilities for Vendors/ Suppliers of large corporates for getting financial liquidity for their supplies made to large corporates.
Payable Finance (Limit on Anchor):
- Our Payable Finance program provides Working Capital Limits for large corporates enabling them optimising their working capital cycle.

title: Dealer Finance — Dealer Finance : Overview (Bank of Baroda)
body:
Dealer Finance : Overview:

- Dealer (Spoke) raises indent to Supplier (Anchor) requesting a consignment of goods. The Supplier (Anchor) raises funding request on Bank’s portal. The validation of the transaction for parameters like availability of credit limit, validity of invoice, overdue position etc. is digitally verified by our Supply Chain Finance system. On successful validation, finance is instantaneously created by the system and disbursement is credited in to the Supplier’s (Anchor’s) account. The Supplier (Anchor) ships the goods on receipt of funds. On due date the Dealer (Spoke) repays into dealer finance account to liquidate the outstanding amount. title: Government Deposit Schemes — NPS Vatsalya Scheme (Bank of Baroda)
body:

- Its objective is to create a pensioned society and encourage the empowerment of children by inculcating the habit of saving for retirement from an early age.
- PRAN is issued in the name of minor.

- Atal Pension Yojana is based on National Pension Scheme.
- APY aims at providing a steady stream of income after the age of 60 to all citizens of India.
- Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) will be provided to the subscriber immediately by the branch.

- Kisan Vikas Patra is a small savings instrument that will facilitate people to invest in a long term savings plan.

body:
Floating Rate Savings Bonds:
- The government has announced the launch of Floating Rate Savings Bonds, 2020 (Taxable). 93 authorized branches of Bank of Baroda have subscription of this scheme.
- No maximum limit for investment in the bonds.
- The interest rate of the bond, would be reset half yearly (in sync with the coupon payment date) @ 35 bps over the respective NSC rate.
Gold Monetization Scheme:
- Gold is mobilized from households and institutions of the country to facilitate its use for productive purposes, and in the long run, to reduce country’s reliance on the import of gold.
- 102 Bank of Baroda branches are authorized to accept gold deposit.
- Rate of interest depends on type of deposit.

title: Government Deposit Schemes — Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (Bank of Baroda)
body:
Senior Citizen Savings Scheme:
- The SCSS account is a robust and safe account designed especially for seniors to earn long term savings in their old age.
- Retired individuals above age of 60 years; or above 55 years of age retired under voluntary or special voluntary scheme or 50 years for the retired personnel of defence services (excluding civil defence employees).
- Depositors are allowed to open multiple account under this scheme with combined maximum limit of Rs. 30 lakhs in all accounts.
Sovereign Gold Bonds:
- A sovereign gold bond is a government security that is denominated in gold grams. Investors invest in these bonds when the scheme opens and it is redeemed on maturity.
- It is a substitute for physical gold.
- Interest of 2.5% paid half yearly for tenure of 8 years.
Public Provident Fund:
- Public Provident Fund (PPF) is an ideal investment option for individuals seeking a secure, low-risk, long-term savings instrument with guaranteed returns.

title: Government Deposit Schemes — Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (Bank of Baroda)
body:
Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana:
- Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana scheme was launched on 02/12/2014 as part of the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao campaign.
- Account holders can earn 8.2% interest on their deposits.
- The depositor must make a deposit of minimum Rs. 250 up to Rs. 1, 50,000 every year until 15 years from the date of account opening.
National Pension Scheme:
- The National Pension System, commonly referred to as NPS, is a voluntary, contribution retirement savings scheme and that has been designed to enable systematic savings during the subscriber's working life. Under the NPS, each subscriber opens an account with the Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA), which is identified through a unique Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN).
- NPS is shaped to enable a systematic savings during the subscribers working life.
- Open an NPS scheme today and be independent.

- All Sovereign Gold Bond (SGB) / RBI Bond investors of Bank of Baroda, particularly those whose interest payments have not been credited and whose bonds have already matured or are due to mature, are requested to visit their respective Bank of Baroda branches on a priority basis and get their bank account linked with the bond. This is essential to ensure timely credit of interest and/or maturity proceeds.
- Bank of Baroda shall not be responsible for any delay caused due to incorrect bank account details or closure of the linked bank account. In cases where the receipt of interest or principal has been delayed for more than six years, the matter shall be dealt with in accordance with RBI guidelines, as available on the RBI website.
- Investors are also advised not to close the bank account linked with the bond, until the bond proceeds are received. If, for any reason, the account needs to be closed, an alternative bank account must first be linked with the bond, and only thereafter should the existing account be closed.

title: Sovereign Gold Bonds — Sovereign Gold Bonds : Features (Bank of Baroda)
body:
Sovereign Gold Bonds : Features:
- The minimum investment that can be made in this bond is 1 gram. Each individual or HUF can hold a maximum of 4 kgs every year in such bonds. For trusts, charitable institutions, the maximum limit is 20 kgs.
- Interest will be earned on the Sovereign Gold Bonds at the rate of 2.5% annually, paid semi-annually.
- The prices of the gold bond are transparent since they are linked to the price of gold in the market.
- There is an exit option for investors after the 5th year of the date of issue of the Bond. Repayments will be done on the next interest payment date.
- The sovereign gold bond offers joint holders and nominees to the investors.
- Bonds held in Demat form are eligible to be traded on the stock exchanges.
- Cash, demand draft, cheques, internet banking/bob World are acceptable modes of payment for the sovereign gold bond scheme, India. However, cash is only accepted up to Rs. 20,000.
